original_value: Since the commercial introduction of Ion Mobility coupled with Mass Spectrometry (IM‐MS) devices in 2003, a large number of research laboratories have embraced the technique. IM‐MS is a fairly rapid experiment used as a molecular separation tool and to obtain structural information. The interpretation of IM‐MS data is still challenging and relies heavily on theoretical calculations of the molecule's collision cross section (CCS) against a buffer gas. Here, a new software (HPCCS) is presented, which performs CCS calculations using high perfomance computing techniques. Based on the trajectory method, HPCCS can accurately calculate CCS for a great variety of molecules, ranging from small organic molecules to large protein complexes, using helium or nitrogen as buffer gas with considerable gains in computer time compared to publicly available codes under the same level of theory. HPCCS is available as free software under the Academic Use License at https://github.com/cepid-cces/hpccs. © 2018 Wiley Periodicals, Inc.

result.paraphrase: Since Ion Mobility coupled with Mass Spectrometry (IM‑MS) devices were commercially introduced in 2003, many research laboratories have adopted the method. IM‑MS is a relatively fast experiment used both for molecular separation and for obtaining structural information. Interpreting IM‑MS data remains difficult and depends heavily on theoretical calculations of a molecule’s collision cross section (CCS) with a buffer gas. This paper presents HPCCS, a new software package that carries out CCS calculations using high-performance computing techniques. Built on the trajectory method, HPCCS can accurately compute CCS for a wide range of molecules, from small organic compounds to large protein complexes, using helium or nitrogen as the buffer gas, while offering substantial reductions in computation time compared with publicly available codes at the same level of theory. HPCCS is free software released under the Academic Use License at https://github.com/cepid-cces/hpccs. © 2018 Wiley Periodicals, Inc.
